venue.name: Morrell Nature Sanctuary
venue.description: Morrell Nature Sanctuary is a 111 hectare second growth forest at 787 Nanaimo Lakes Road, run by a volunteer society on land owned by The Nature Trust of British Columbia. There is no admission fee, the gates are open daily from 7am to 9pm, and there are 11km of trails, washrooms at the entrance, a sheltered picnic area at Morrell Lake and a wheelchair accessible Yew Loop trail. Trained volunteer nature interpreters run booked field trips for kindergarten to grade 7, priced at $60 or $65 depending on the length of the walk. Guided walks can also be arranged for other groups, and summer day camps run for children aged 5 to 12.
venue.address: 787 Nanaimo Lakes Road, Nanaimo, BC V9R 3C2

facility_notes.washrooms: There are restroom facilities at the entrance, and at the sheltered picnic area at Morrell Lake.
facility_notes.lunch_space: There are picnic benches at the entrance, and viewing benches located throughout our 11km of trails. Visitors are welcome to bring their own food and drinks. However, they are responsible for carrying out any garbage they generate.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: To the left of the entrance gate is the "Yew Loop" trail, built for wheelchair accessibility.
facility_notes.bus_parking: Groups are required to park in the overflow lot at Nanaimo Lakes Road to avoid congestion in the parking area.

restrictions: No harvesting is permitted within Sanctuary grounds.
Bicycles are not allowed on any Sanctuary trail.
All dogs must be on leash at Morrell Nature Sanctuary at all times. Please clean up after your dogs.
Morrell Programs will be run rain or shine, unless there are high winds.
venue.hours_notes: Our gates are open daily from 7:00am to 9:00pm for your exploration and enjoyment. The office is staffed Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday 8:30am to 4:00pm and Monday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday 10am to 2pm.
venue.seasonal_notes: Seeds and Spores is offered in the fall only. Pond Dippers and Mother Nature's Riches are offered in spring. The other field trips are listed as all year. Fall trips are booked in September and spring trips in late January.
venue.price_year_or_season: Fall 2026 school programs; spring 2027 listed as coming soon

programs.name: Nature Walk, Exploring the Forest
programs.description: A two hour walk in field trip for grades 3 to 7, offered all year. It looks at the Coastal Douglas-fir ecosystem and the relationship between plants, animals and non-living things, and the flyer says it also shows students how to identify seven of the most common trees in the forest. The fee is $65 and we have read that as a charge for the class rather than per student.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the forest trails for about two hours with a trained volunteer interpreter, stopping to look at trees, plants and signs of animals and learning to tell seven common trees apart.
programs.our_note: This is the two hour walking version, so children are on their feet on uneven forest trail for most of it. Trips run rain or shine unless it is windy, so send everyone in boots and rain gear and expect mud.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are at the entrance and at the Morrell Lake picnic shelter, and there are picnic benches to eat at. Nobody has published how many adults you need to bring or whether a bus can turn around, so ask when you book.
programs.evidence: NATURE WALK Grades 3-7 Walk in - 2 hours $65.00

programs.name: Seeds and Spores
programs.description: A fall only field trip about seasonal change and plant life cycles, looking at which plants make seeds and which make spores and how animals and plants depend on each other. It comes in two lengths. Grades K to 2 do a 1.5 hour drive in version for $60 and grades 3 to 7 do a 2 hour walk in version for $65. We have read those fees as a charge for the class rather than per student.
programs.what_children_do: Walk into the forest with a volunteer interpreter and look closely at the plants that are making seeds and spores at that time of year, comparing what the different plants are doing.
programs.our_note: The younger version is called drive in, which means you go in by vehicle rather than walking the whole way, and it is half an hour shorter. If you have a mixed age group, ask which version they will run before you book.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are at the entrance and at the Morrell Lake picnic shelter, and there are picnic benches for lunch. How many adults you need is not published, so settle that on the phone.
programs.extra_fees_note: The longer two hour walk in version for grades 3 to 7 is $65 rather than $60.
programs.evidence: SEEDS & SPORES (Change of Season) Gr. K-2 Drive in - 1.5 hours $60.00 Gr. 3-7 Walk in - 2 hours $65.00

programs.name: Forest Detectives
programs.description: Students hunt for signs of biodiversity in the forest using observation, investigation and deduction. It comes in two lengths. Grades K to 2 do a 1.5 hour drive in version for $60 and grades 3 to 7 do a 2 hour walk in version for $65. We have read those fees as a charge for the class rather than per student. Their own pages give two different grade ranges for this one, so check which grades they will take.
programs.what_children_do: Search the forest floor and the trees for clues about the animals and plants that live there, then work out what left them.
programs.our_note: This is the one that lands best with children who like a hunt rather than a lecture. The shorter drive in version is the one to ask for with a young group, because the walking version is a full two hours on trail.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are at the entrance and at the Morrell Lake picnic shelter and there are picnic benches to eat at. How many adults have to come is not published anywhere, so ask when you book.
programs.extra_fees_note: The longer two hour walk in version for grades 3 to 7 is $65 rather than $60.
programs.evidence: FOREST DETECTIVES Gr. K-2 Drive in - 1.5 hours-$60.00 Gr. 3-7 Walk in - 2 hours -$65.00

programs.name: Exploring Nature
programs.description: A short 1.5 hour nature walk for kindergarten to grade 2, offered all year. It follows the trails looking at seasonal change and at local plants and animals, and the children are asked to use their senses to explore. The fee is $60 and we have read that as a charge for the class rather than per student.
programs.what_children_do: Follow the trails with a volunteer interpreter for about an hour and a half, stopping to touch, smell and listen to what is around them and to notice what has changed with the season.
programs.our_note: This is the shortest of their trips and the only one written for the youngest grades, so it is the one to start with. It is a drive in trip, meaning you do not walk the whole way in from the gate.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are at the entrance and at the Morrell Lake picnic shelter and there are picnic benches for lunch. Nothing is published about how many adults you need or where a bus parks, so ask.
programs.evidence: EXPLORING NATURE Grades K-2 Drive in - 1.5 hour $60.00

programs.name: Pond Dippers, Introduction to Life in the Pond
programs.description: A spring field trip at the pond. Children dip for and collect specimens and then talk about life cycles, adaptations and how to tell the creatures apart. Kindergarten and grade 1 do a 1.5 hour drive in version for $60 and grade 2 and up do a 2 hour walk in version for $65. We have read those fees as a charge for the class rather than per student. Spring 2027 dates were still listed as coming soon when we looked.
programs.what_children_do: Kneel at the edge of the pond, dip and collect creatures from the water, then look at what they caught and talk about how those animals live and grow.
programs.our_note: This is the one where children have their hands in the water, so bring spare socks and a change of clothes for the small ones. It runs in spring only and the spring dates were not up yet when we looked, so put a note in your calendar for late January.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are at the entrance and at the Morrell Lake picnic shelter and there are picnic benches to eat at. How many adults have to come is not published, so ask when you book.
programs.extra_fees_note: The longer two hour walk in version for grade 2 and up is $65 rather than $60.
programs.evidence: K-1 Drive-in - 1.5 hours - $60 Gr 2 & up Walk-in - 2 hours - $65

programs.name: Mother Nature's Riches
programs.description: A spring walk in field trip for grades 3 to 7 about Traditional Ecological Knowledge and the plants that were once vitally important to the Coast Salish Peoples of British Columbia. It runs two hours and the fee is $65, which we have read as a charge for the class rather than per student. Spring 2027 dates were still listed as coming soon when we looked.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the trails for about two hours with a volunteer interpreter, stopping at particular plants to hear what they were used for by the Coast Salish Peoples.
programs.our_note: It is a two hour walk with a lot of listening, so it suits older classes who can hold attention on trail. Spring dates were not posted when we looked, so ask in late January.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are at the entrance and at the Morrell Lake picnic shelter and there are picnic benches for lunch. How many adults you need is not published, so settle it when you book.
programs.evidence: Spring - Gr. 3-7 This program will focus on the concepts of Traditional Ecological Knowledge

programs.name: Guided group tour
programs.description: A guided walk led by an experienced nature interpreter, arranged by contacting the office. It is offered for up to 15 people with a suggested donation of $65 for the group. The sanctuary does not publish how long it lasts or what ages it suits.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the forest trails with an interpreter who stops along the way to point out how the forest fits together.
programs.our_note: This is the route for a group that is not a school class, a daycare outing for instance. The 15 person limit is small, so a bigger group will need to be split or booked as two visits.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are at the entrance and at the Morrell Lake picnic shelter and there are picnic benches to eat at. No age limit, length or start time is published, so all of that has to be agreed with the office.
programs.extra_fees_note: The $65 is written as a suggested donation for the group, not a fixed fee.
programs.evidence: You can schedule by contacting our office, for up to 15 individuals, with a suggested donation of $65 per group.

programs.name: Self guided group visit
programs.description: Anyone can walk the sanctuary free of charge from 7am to 9pm. A gathering of 10 or more counts as a group and the sanctuary asks to be told in advance by email, with your name, the date and time, the number of people and any accessibility needs. For groups over 10 they recommend a donation of $65. Groups must park in the overflow lot on Nanaimo Lakes Road, and booked school programs get first call on the benches and learning circles.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the sanctuary's 11km of trails at their own pace, including the level Yew Loop near the gate, stopping at the benches and the picnic shelter at Morrell Lake.
programs.our_note: If you are bringing vulnerable children or anyone with allergies, their own guidance asks you to book a guided tour instead of coming on your own. Tell them you are coming even though it is free, because a booked school group has priority on the picnic shelter and the learning circles.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms at the entrance and at the Morrell Lake shelter, picnic benches for lunch and a level Yew Loop trail for wheels. There is no rain shelter beyond the picnic area and no published bus parking, so plan for weather and check parking first.
programs.extra_fees_note: For groups larger than 10 individuals, we politely recommend a donation of $65 to Morrell Sanctuary Society for Environmental Education.
programs.evidence: A "group" is defined as: a gathering of 10 or more individuals visiting the Sanctuary together for any purpose.

gaps: Price: the school programs pages and the field trip flyer give $60 and $65 but never say in words whether that is per class or per student. We have recorded it as a charge for the class, because their group visit guidelines price a guided tour at $65 per group and because the same pages recommend a class size of 20 to 24. Confirm it when you book.

Youngest age: everything for schools is written in grades, from kindergarten upwards, and no minimum age is published. The site never mentions preschool or daycare groups, so we have not answered whether daycares are hosted.
How many adults have to come: not published anywhere. No ratio, no free chaperone count, no adult price for any field trip.
Lead time: no minimum notice is published. The pages only say fall trips are booked in September and spring trips in late January.

Capacity: the recommended maximum of 20 to 24 students per class is written as a recommendation for interpreter quality, not as a hard limit, so treat the 24 we recorded as their guidance rather than a rule.

Rain backup: field trips run rain or shine unless there are high winds, and no indoor alternative is described. There is a Woods Room education building mentioned in a donation thank you note, but no page says a group can shelter in it.
Bus parking: not addressed. Groups are told to use the overflow lot on Nanaimo Lakes Road, but nothing says whether a school bus can get in or turn around.
Start times: no time slots are published for any field trip.
Months: unknown for Seeds and Spores, Pond Dippers and Mother Nature's Riches. The site says fall only or spring without naming months, so months have been left blank rather than guessed.
Spring 2027 field trips were still marked coming soon when we looked, and the spring block on the school programs page still shows last year's grade bands.

The about page says the society earns fees from in class presentations to students by trained interpreters, but no page describes that offering, so we have not listed it as a bookable program. Worth asking about if you want them to come to you.
The School Registration link in the site menu goes to a page that no longer exists. Fall trips are booked through the registration link on the school programs page.

Summer day camps for ages 5 to 12 run at $45 per day with a maximum of 24 campers, but they are registered child by child rather than booked as a group, so they are not listed as a program here. The 2026 season had already finished when we looked.

The map on the home page is only scrolled to a point near the sanctuary rather than pinned to it, so the coordinates here come from the street address instead. That address is the sanctuary building and parking area at the Nanaimo Lakes Road entrance, which is the right place to send a bus, but the sanctuary itself covers 111 hectares.

The site is built in Xara and its photographs are numbered files with no alt text, and the school programs photograph is a background image rather than an ordinary picture. Both images here were opened in a browser and looked at before their descriptions were written.

conflicts.note: Their school programs page lists Forest Detectives twice and gives two different answers for which grades it is for. One says kindergarten to grade 7, the other says grades 3 to 7. Their fall flyer says kindergarten to grade 7, which is what we have used, so it is worth confirming your grade when you book.
